webhooks.summary: Figma provides a webhook system via its REST API v2. You create webhooks programmatically (POST /v2/webhooks) specifying an endpoint URL and one or more event types. Figma then delivers POST requests to that endpoint when events fire. A PING event is sent automatically on creation (unless the webhook is created in a PAUSED state). Failed deliveries are retried 3 times with exponential backoff.

events.name: PING
events.description: Triggers when a webhook is created. Used for debugging. Cannot be subscribed to — all webhooks receive PING events on creation (unless created in PAUSED status).

events.name: FILE_UPDATE
events.description: Triggers within 30 minutes of editing inactivity in a file. Subscribing to FILE_UPDATE also automatically delivers FILE_DELETE events.

events.name: FILE_VERSION_UPDATE
events.description: Triggers whenever a named version is created in the version history of a file.

events.name: FILE_DELETE
events.description: Triggers whenever a file has been deleted. Automatically received if subscribed to FILE_UPDATE. Does not trigger for files inside a deleted folder.

events.name: LIBRARY_PUBLISH
events.description: Triggers whenever a library file is published. A separate event fires for each library asset type (components, styles, variables) that has changes.

events.name: FILE_COMMENT
events.description: Triggers when someone comments on a file.

events.name: DEV_MODE_STATUS_UPDATE
events.description: Triggers whenever the Dev Mode status for a layer in a file changes.

managementEndpoints.description: Create a webhook. Specify endpoint URL, event types, and scope (file or team). Sends a PING on creation unless status is set to PAUSED.
List webhooks by context or plan. For plan scope, returns webhooks across all accessible contexts; response is paginated.
Get a single webhook by ID.
Update a webhook by ID (e.g., change endpoint, events, or status).
Delete a webhook by ID. Irreversible.
[Deprecated] Returns all webhooks registered under the specified team.
Returns all webhook requests sent within the last week. Useful for debugging delivery issues.

signature.detail: No signature verification header or HMAC scheme is documented in the provided OpenAPI specification. The spec does not reference any webhook-signature, X-Figma-Signature, or comparable header for authenticating inbound payloads. Implementations relying solely on the provided spec cannot cryptographically verify that a request originated from Figma.

setupSteps.title: Obtain your inbound hook URL
setupSteps.detail: Retrieve the stable inbound webhook URL assigned to your workspace in the package registry. This is the URL Figma will POST event payloads to.

setupSteps.title: Prepare your Figma credentials
setupSteps.detail: You need either a Figma Personal Access Token or an OAuth2 token with the `webhooks:write` scope. Both authentication methods are supported across all webhook operations.

setupSteps.title: Identify the target scope
setupSteps.detail: Determine whether the webhook should cover a specific file or an entire team. Figma webhook subscriptions are scoped to a file key or a team ID. Collect the relevant file key or team ID from Figma.

setupSteps.title: Create the webhook via the Figma API
setupSteps.detail:
Send a POST request to /v2/webhooks with a JSON body containing: the endpoint URL (your registry inbound hook URL), the event_type(s) you want to subscribe to (e.g., FILE_UPDATE, FILE_COMMENT, LIBRARY_PUBLISH), the file_key or team_id scope, and optionally a status of PAUSED if you do not want an automatic PING on creation.

Example:
curl -X POST https://api.figma.com/v2/webhooks \
  -H "X-Figma-Token: <YOUR_TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"event_type":"FILE_UPDATE","team_id":"<TEAM_ID>","endpoint":"<YOUR_REGISTRY_HOOK_URL>"}'

setupSteps.title: Verify the PING event
setupSteps.detail: Unless the webhook was created in PAUSED status, Figma immediately sends a PING event to your endpoint. Confirm your registry inbound hook URL responds with HTTP 200. If your server returns a non-200 status or times out, Figma retries 3 times with exponential backoff. You can inspect delivery results via GET /v2/webhooks/{webhook_id}/requests, which returns requests from the last week.

setupSteps.title: Confirm registration in the registry webhooks area
setupSteps.detail: Once the PING (or first event) is received successfully, verify in the package registry's webhooks area that the hook URL is registered and active. The inbound hook URL provided by the registry is now wired to Figma event delivery.
